avoid.reason: The Pioneer Park / Rio Grande blocks and stretches of North Temple feel sketchy after dark due to concentrated homelessness and drug activity.

hood_desc: The walkable core around Temple Square, City Creek Center, and the Delta Center; home to the main TRAX lines, the Free Fare Zone, and most big hotels, making it the easiest base for first-timers.
A historic hillside grid of Victorian homes, leafy streets, and small cafes just northeast of downtown; quiet, residential, and popular with locals and university students.
A laid-back, family-friendly neighborhood built around Sugar House Park and Westminster University, with local breweries, shops, and a relaxed pace away from downtown.
A fast-changing former industrial area just south of downtown filled with craft breweries, distilleries, art studios, and new restaurants; the heart of SLC's maker scene.

transit.hours: TRAX and buses run roughly 5am to midnight; FrontRunner runs early morning to about 11pm on weekdays with limited Saturday service and no Sunday service.
transit.pay: Tap a contactless bank card or phone, or a FAREPAY card, at TRAX and FrontRunner platforms and on buses. A single UTA bus or TRAX fare is $2.50; FrontRunner is distance-based. Downtown's Free Fare Zone lets you ride TRAX free between North Temple and 900 South.

food.name: Pastrami Burger
food.desc: Utah's own invention from the city's Greek-American diners: a charbroiled patty buried under a pile of griddled pastrami, cheese and special sauce.

places.name: Crown Burgers
places.area: Multiple, including Emigration Canyon and Highland Drive
places.note: The undisputed original; makes its pastrami in house at seven Salt Lake area locations.

places.name: Yanni's Family Restaurant
places.note: Single-location Greek-American fast food joint slinging pastrami burgers for decades.

places.name: Apollo Burger
places.area: Multiple, across the Salt Lake Valley
places.note: Local rival with a slightly different, saucier take on the pastrami burger.

food.name: Funeral Potatoes
food.desc: Shredded potato baked with cheese, sour cream and onion under a crunchy cornflake crust. Named for the church-hall gatherings it feeds.

places.name: Garage on Beck
places.note: Serves an elevated version with a crisp golden topping; the best-known restaurant take.

places.name: Ruth's Diner
places.note: Canyon comfort-food institution where Utah casseroles turn up beside the eggs.

places.name: Harmons City Creek
places.note: Utah grocery chain whose deli counter sells funeral potatoes by the tray, ready to eat.

food.name: Utah Scone with Honey Butter
food.desc: Nothing like a British scone: a pillow of deep-fried dough that puffs up hot and gets slathered with honey butter.

places.name: Ruth's Diner
places.note: Famous mile-high scone arrives with every breakfast; the standard order since 1930.

places.name: Sconecutter
places.note: Long-running late-night scone shop that also stuffs them into sandwiches.

places.name: Utah State Fairpark stands
places.note: Seasonal fair and rodeo stands still fry the classic honey-butter scone.

food.name: Fry Sauce
food.desc: The pink Utah condiment, roughly ketchup and mayonnaise with secret extras, invented in Salt Lake City in the 1950s. Ask for it with everything.

places.name: Arctic Circle
places.area: Multiple, across the Salt Lake Valley
places.note: The chain that first put fry sauce on the counter and still sets the standard.

places.name: Hires Big H
places.note: Drive-in institution since 1959; root beer, burgers and its own fry sauce recipe.

places.name: Crown Burgers
places.note: Fry sauce comes with the fries by default alongside the pastrami burger.

food.name: Greek-American Souvlaki and Gyros
food.desc: Salt Lake's Greek immigrant families shaped its diners. Skewered pork, lemon and oregano, wrapped in pita or plated with rice and salad.

places.name: Manoli's
places.note: Modern Greek small plates from a Salt Lake Greek family; one of the city's best-reviewed rooms.

places.name: Aristo's
places.note: Long-standing Greek restaurant with a shaded patio and proper charcoal-grilled souvlaki.

places.name: Greek Souvlaki
places.note: No-frills local chain that has fed the city cheap gyros and souvlaki for decades.

food.name: Rocky Mountain Trout
food.desc: Pan-seared or wood-grilled trout from the Wasatch streams, usually finished with brown butter, almonds or lemon. The mountain-town classic.

places.name: Log Haven
places.note: Log-mansion restaurant beside a waterfall, 20 minutes up the canyon; special-occasion cooking.

places.name: Market Street Grill
places.note: City seafood standby that has run fresh fish, including trout, since 1980.

places.name: Ruth's Diner
places.note: Casual canyon option for trout and eggs on the creekside patio.

food.name: Dirty Soda
food.desc: A Utah phenomenon: fountain soda loaded with coconut syrup, cream and fruit puree over pebble ice. Big, sweet and entirely alcohol-free.

places.name: Swig
places.area: Multiple, across the Salt Lake Valley
places.note: The Utah chain that started the dirty soda craze; drive-through only at most locations.

places.name: Sodalicious
places.note: Rival soda shop with cheekily named combinations and a big cookie counter.

places.name: FiiZ Drinks
places.note: Third of the big three soda shops, with the widest syrup list of the lot.

food.name: Utah Craft Beer
food.desc: Utah's liquor rules cap draft beer at a lower strength, which has pushed local brewers toward genuinely good sessionable lagers and pilsners.

places.name: Fisher Brewing Company
places.note: Worker-owned taproom reviving an 1880s Salt Lake brewery name; food trucks outside.

places.name: Squatters Pub Brewery
places.note: The city's original brewpub, open since 1989 and still a dependable pint and burger.

places.name: TF Brewing
places.note: German-leaning lagers and a big beer garden; among the most praised brewers in the state.

landmarks: Salt Lake Temple
The six-spired granite temple at the heart of Temple Square is the most iconic symbol of Salt Lake City and the LDS Church worldwide.
Utah State Capitol
A stately Renaissance Revival building with a copper dome, perched on a hill offering commanding views over downtown Salt Lake City.
Salt Lake Tabernacle
The distinctive dome-roofed hall on Temple Square is famed for its remarkable acoustics and home of the Tabernacle Choir.
Great Salt Lake
The largest saltwater lake in the Western Hemisphere produces surreal mirror-like sunsets over the surrounding mountains.
This Is the Place Heritage Park
A living-history pioneer village marking where Brigham Young's Mormon pioneers first entered the Salt Lake Valley in 1847.
Cathedral of the Madeleine
A striking Gothic Revival Catholic cathedral with an ornate painted interior, a beautiful architectural counterpoint to the city's LDS landmarks.
Antelope Island State Park
A rugged island reached by causeway across the Great Salt Lake, home to free-roaming bison herds and dramatic lakeside vistas.
Natural History Museum of Utah
The striking, rock-clad Rio Tinto Center building blends into the foothills and houses dinosaur fossils and Utah's natural wonders.
Gilgal Sculpture Garden
A quirky, hidden garden of surreal Mormon-themed stone sculptures, including a sphinx with Joseph Smith's face, tucked behind downtown.
Spiral Jetty
Robert Smithson's monumental 1970 earthwork coiling into the Great Salt Lake's pink-tinged water is one of the world's most famous land art pieces.

train.note: No international trains run anywhere near Utah. Amtrak's California Zephyr is the only intercity service, calling once a day in each direction at the Salt Lake City Intermodal Hub on 300 South 600 West - westbound to Reno, Sacramento and Emeryville, eastbound over the Rockies to Denver and Chicago. Both calls fall in the middle of the night and the train is often well behind schedule, so arrange a taxi rather than relying on connections. UTA's FrontRunner commuter rail is far more useful day to day, running north to Ogden and south to Provo from the same hub.

bus.note: No international coaches. Greyhound (https://www.greyhound.com/) and FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/) use the Intermodal Hub for services to Las Vegas in 7-8 hours, Denver in about 11, plus Reno and Boise. Salt Lake Express (https://saltlakeexpress.com/) is the regional workhorse, running daily shuttles from the airport and downtown to more than 50 towns across Utah, Idaho, Wyoming, Montana and Nevada, including Idaho Falls, West Yellowstone and Jackson. Book Salt Lake Express online in advance, as many runs are small vans that fill up.

ferry.note: There are no ferries. The Great Salt Lake is too shallow and saline for scheduled passenger service, and falling water levels have repeatedly left its marinas dry.

half.name: Park City
half.blurb: A former silver-mining town about 35 minutes away is now a ski resort town that hosted events during the 2002 Winter Olympics.

half.name: Timpanogos Cave National Monument
half.blurb: A cave system about 50 minutes away is reached by a steep mile-and-a-half trail leading to chambers of colorful stalactites and helictites.

half.name: Bingham Canyon Mine
half.blurb: An open-pit copper mine about 40 minutes away is one of the largest man-made excavations on earth, visible from an overlook.

half.name: Provo
half.blurb: A university city about 45 minutes away is home to Brigham Young University and sits at the base of the Wasatch Range.

full.name: Bonneville Salt Flats
full.blurb: A vast white salt pan about two hours west has hosted land-speed racing since the early 20th century.
